display_title: Omics-based molecular classifications empowering in precision oncology
summary: Narrative review connecting molecular biomarkers, single- and multi-omics cancer classification, biomarker-oriented trial designs and translational constraints; it provides no new patient cohort or pooled treatment effect.
research_question: How does omics-based molecular classification connect cancer diagnosis, treatment stratification and prognosis, and what limits its clinical translation?
author_summary: This narrative review organizes published work around molecular diagnosis, treatment stratification and prognosis. It covers genomic and epigenomic, transcriptomic and proteomic biomarkers, then discusses integrated and spatial omics as ways to characterize tumor heterogeneity. A separate section compares biomarker-oriented clinical-trial designs. The final sections address data integration, algorithm interpretability and the limitations of preclinical tumor models. These are a synthesis and research agenda: clinical effects and model performance described in the review belong to the cited studies, not to a new cohort or validation experiment conducted for this article.
evidence_page_notice: Evidence synthesis of a published narrative review. The reviewed full text is the publicly readable text of an author-uploaded typeset copy on ResearchGate, matched to the publisher's article identity. It is not a new clinical study, and the reviewed copy has not been verified byte-for-byte against the publisher PDF.

what_this_adds: An organized route from omics biomarker classes to molecular stratification and clinical-study design.
A secondary-literature framework that separates the promise of integration from the need for interpretable algorithms, suitable models and clinical validation.

supports: A conceptual overview of omics biomarker layers and molecular classification in oncology.
Context for discussing biomarker-oriented trial designs and translation challenges.
does_not_establish: A new patient cohort, newly validated classifier or new therapeutic experiment.
A pooled treatment effect, diagnostic accuracy or causal benefit of molecular classification.
Clinical superiority of multi-omics for every cancer or independent confirmation of all cited primary-study results.
Systematic completeness of the literature search or a meta-analysis.

qa.question: Which biomarker layers are distinguished in the review?
qa.answer: Its biomarker overview distinguishes genomic, epigenomic, transcriptomic and proteomic information. These are categories of prior molecular research, not four new validation cohorts.

qa.question: Does this review validate a new multi-omics classifier?
qa.answer: No. It discusses published integration and spatial-profiling approaches. Performance or treatment-response claims for any particular classifier must be checked in the cited primary study.

qa.question: Which clinical-trial design frameworks are compared?
qa.answer: The review compares basket, umbrella, platform and N-of-1 designs. This comparison provides context for molecularly informed trial design; it does not supply a pooled efficacy estimate.

qa.question: What prevents a molecular classification from automatically becoming a treatment recommendation?
qa.answer: The review identifies complex data integration, the need for clinical interpretability and limitations of preclinical models. Its discussion of AI, organoids and three-dimensional models is a research agenda, not clinical proof of benefit.

limitations: This is a narrative synthesis without a reported systematic search or pooled effect estimation.
Results from cited cohorts, trials and experiments remain secondary evidence here; no new primary cohort or validation is reported.

The public ResearchGate text reproduces a typeset copy uploaded by Zhaokai Zhou on 2 February 2024. The publisher record confirms article identity, but publisher-PDF byte equivalence was not verified.

Only structural and qualitative review claims are summarized. Numerical results from individual cited studies and the table's assignment of particular trials to design categories are not independently validated.

related_papers.relationship: Complementary narrative review focused on proteomic measurement and integration; related conceptual context, not independent clinical validation.

provenance.visual_verification_scope: Official public thumbnail images of Figs. 1, 3 and 4 were inspected for schematic subject matter and agree with the captions. No effect size or performance value was read from an image. All selected claims are supported by the readable body/table text.
provenance.reuse_boundary: Publisher states exclusive rights; no open reuse license was verified. This page contains original, bounded paraphrases only and does not redistribute the PDF or figures.
provenance.correction_check: Official publisher article and same-day Crossref metadata were checked. No correction relation was returned or displayed in the inspected records; this is not an exhaustive guarantee that no later update exists.
